title: Demystifying Synthetic Data in LLM Pre-training: A Systematic Study of Scaling Laws, Benefits, and Pitfalls
why: Surfaced by the 2026-07-04 freshness sweep as the closest empirical precedent to B6.2's core question: a >1000-model, unified-protocol sweep of synthetic-fraction mixture ratio in real LM pretraining, explicitly engaging and partially rejecting 'model collapse' generalizability. Read in full (not from a search snippet) and confirmed NOT a preempting method-twin: it is benefit/efficiency-framed (optimal ratio for training speed/loss, single-round n=1, scaling-law curve-fitting), with no formal change-point/threshold statistical test, no confound isolation via entropy-matched human control, no detector-based dose-measurement-error correction, and explicit self-stated Limitations declining multi-generational dynamics and fine-grained capability-battery evaluation -- exactly the gaps B6.2's harm-framed, statistically-adjudicated dose-response design fills. Concede-and-differentiate treatment in Related Work, not a repositioning trigger (guidance.md Part 4 situation 6 does not apply).

title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
why: Phase-A-followup fix (2026-07-04): cited by name with specific claims in paper_draft.tex's Related Work ('shows this can be avoided if synthetic data accumulates alongside real data rather than replacing it') but had no reference-cache record -- a hard-gate violation.
